Fungal infection.description: A fungal infection, also known as mycosis, is a disease caused by a fungus. Infections can appear on the skin, nails, lungs, or bloodstream.

Allergy.description: An allergy is an immune system response to a foreign substance. Allergens include pollen, dust mites, pet dander, insect stings, foods, and medications.
precautions: Keep windows closed during high pollen season

GERD.description: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a chronic digestive disease where stomach acid flows back into the esophagus, causing irritation.

Chronic cholestasis.description: A condition where bile flow from the liver is reduced or blocked, causing bile to build up in the liver and bloodstream.

Drug Reaction.description: An adverse drug reaction is an unintended, harmful response to a medication taken at normal doses.
precautions: Inform your doctor about all medications

Peptic ulcer disease.description: Open sores that develop on the inner lining of the stomach and the upper portion of the small intestine. Often caused by H. pylori bacteria or NSAIDs.

AIDS.description: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is the final stage of HIV infection that occurs when the body's immune system is badly damaged by the virus.

Diabetes.description: A group of diseases that result in too much sugar in the blood (high blood glucose). Type 1 is autoimmune; Type 2 is lifestyle-related.

Gastroenteritis.description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, typically resulting from a bacterial or viral infection. Also called stomach flu.

Bronchial Asthma.description: A condition where airways narrow, swell, and may produce extra mucus, making breathing difficult. Triggers include allergens, exercise, and cold air.

Hypertension.description: High blood pressure is a common condition where the long-term force of blood against artery walls is high enough to eventually cause health problems.

Migraine.description: A neurological condition characterized by intense, debilitating headaches, often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound.

Cervical spondylosis.description: Age-related wear and tear affecting the spinal disks in the neck. Can cause neck pain and stiffness, and sometimes pressure on the spinal cord or nerve roots.

Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).description: Loss of muscle function in part of the body due to bleeding in or around the brain. This is a medical emergency.

Jaundice.description: Yellowing of the skin and whites of the eyes caused by high levels of bilirubin. It can signal liver, gallbladder, or bile duct problems.

Malaria.description: A disease caused by a Plasmodium parasite transmitted by infected Anopheles mosquitoes. Causes cycles of fever and chills.
precautions: Use insect repellent and bed nets

Chicken pox.description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy, blister-like rash on the skin. Caused by the varicella-zoster virus.

Dengue.description: A mosquito-borne tropical disease caused by the dengue virus. Causes severe flu-like illness with high fever and pain behind the eyes.

Typhoid.description: A bacterial infection due to Salmonella typhi. Spreads through contaminated food and water, causing high fever, weakness, and stomach pain.

hepatitis A.description: A highly contagious liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus, usually spread through contaminated food or water.

Hepatitis B.description: A serious liver infection caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV). Can become chronic and lead to liver failure, cancer, or cirrhosis.

Hepatitis C.description: A viral infection causing liver inflammation, sometimes leading to serious liver damage. Spread through contact with contaminated blood.

Hepatitis D.description: A serious liver disease caused by the hepatitis D virus (HDV). It only infects people already infected with hepatitis B.

Hepatitis E.description: A liver disease caused by the hepatitis E virus, spread mainly through contaminated water. Usually self-limiting in healthy adults.

Alcoholic hepatitis.description: Inflammation of the liver caused by drinking too much alcohol. Can lead to liver failure in severe cases.

Tuberculosis.description: A potentially serious infectious disease that mainly affects the lungs. Caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and spread through the air.

Common Cold.description: A viral infectious disease of the upper respiratory tract that primarily affects the nose. Caused by rhinovirus.

Pneumonia.description: An infection that inflames air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid. Can range from mild to life-threatening.

Dimorphic hemmorhoids (piles).description: Swollen veins in the anus and lower rectum, similar to varicose veins. Can be internal or external.

Heart attack.description: A heart attack occurs when blood flow that brings oxygen to the heart muscle is severely reduced or cut off completely. This is a medical emergency.

Varicose veins.description: Gnarled, enlarged veins near the surface of the skin. They're most common in the legs and feet.

Hypothyroidism.description: A condition where the thyroid gland doesn't produce enough thyroid hormone. Causes fatigue, weight gain, and cold sensitivity.
precautions: Take thyroid hormone replacement as prescribed

Hyperthyroidism.description: A condition in which the thyroid gland produces too much thyroid hormone. Causes weight loss, rapid heart rate, and anxiety.

Hypoglycemia.description: A condition characterized by abnormally low blood sugar (glucose) levels. Common in people with diabetes.

Osteoarthritis.description: The most common form of arthritis, occurring when the protective cartilage that cushions the ends of bones wears down over time.

Arthritis.description: Inflammation of one or more joints, causing pain and stiffness that can worsen with age. Many types exist including rheumatoid and psoriatic.

(Vertigo) Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo.description: A sudden sensation that you're spinning or that the inside of your head is spinning. Triggered by specific changes in head position.

Acne.description: A skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells. Causes whiteheads, blackheads, and pimples.
precautions: Wash face twice daily with mild cleanser

Urinary tract infection.description: An infection in any part of the urinary system — kidneys, bladder, ureters, and urethra. Most infections involve the lower urinary tract.

Psoriasis.description: A skin disease that causes a rash with itchy, scaly patches, most commonly on the knees, elbows, trunk, and scalp.

Impetigo.description: A highly contagious skin infection that mainly affects infants and children. Causes red sores that can break open, ooze fluid, and develop a honey-colored crust.
